What is Brier score?

Brier score measures the accuracy of probabilistic predictions. A perfect forecaster scores 0; a forecaster who always guesses 50/50 on binary questions scores 0.25; a forecaster who is reliably wrong scores 1. Lower is better. We use Brier rather than profit because it rewards calibration over luck — being right with appropriate confidence, repeatedly. See full methodology.

How to climb the leaderboard

  • Predict consistently — only resolved markets count, and you need 25 to qualify for ranking
  • Calibration matters more than direction — say 70% if you mean 70%, not 95%
  • Specialise — separate leaderboards for Politics, Fiscal, Policy reward depth
  • Streaks are bonus signal, not scoring — 5+ consecutive correct adds visibility

d.title: How we build every Echo
d.lead: Every Echo follows the same six-step process. Pattern recognition over opinion. Multiple sources over single citation. Verified before published, not after.
d.body:
The TEE pattern

Every body paragraph in every Echo follows the same structure: Topic, Evidence, Explanatory. A topic sentence states the claim. Evidence supports it with citation. An explanatory line ties it back to the central pattern. This is the same discipline used in academic essay writing — and it gates editorial quality before publication.

The six-step Echo pipeline

1
Source ingestion
30+ UK and international publications via APIs, scrapers, and archived databases. Hansard (Parliament record from 1803), UK National Archives, ONS, Bank of England, plus broadsheet press archives back to 1900.
2
Pattern detection
AI classifies current events into recurring patterns identified from the historical archive. Bills with similar dynamics. Polling collapses that preceded reshuffles. Policy announcements that fit "wind-down" trajectories. Pattern library at /patterns.
3
Echo draft generation
First draft written in TEE format across three blocks: today's news, historical pattern with cases, market hypothesis with base rates. Each paragraph cited inline (Harvard style).
4
Dual verification
Every factual claim cross-checked across minimum 2 independent sources. Different publications, not multiple copies of the same wire report. Statistics confirmed from authoritative source (ONS, Bank of England, IFS, etc.). Discrepancies flagged for editorial review.
5
Anti-fake check
Automated classifier flags retracted claims, known hoaxes, and AI-generated noise. Cross-reference against Snopes, FactCheck, and publication retraction databases. Anything flagged routed to editor.
6
Editorial pass
Human editor reviews draft for tone, factual nuance, and Editorial Code compliance. No Echo publishes without explicit editor sign-off. Editor's name appears on every Echo.

Numbers

  • 125 years of UK political news archive coverage
  • 30+ publications referenced across each Echo
  • 3 minimum independent sources per factual claim
  • ~3-5 Echoes published per week post-launch
  • 24-hour latency from event to Echo publication (target)

What we will NOT do

  • Publish opinion without evidence backing
  • Take partisan editorial positions on policy questions
  • Use direct quotes from primary sources without paraphrasing the analysis in our own words
  • Recommend market positions (we publish predictions, you make decisions)
  • Trade against our own published markets

Read Editorial Code See all sources

How sources are used

Every Echo references a minimum of 3 of these publications, with at least one primary source (Hansard, ONS, government press release) and at least two independent secondary sources (named publications). The full citation list appears at the foot of every Echo, formatted in Harvard reference style.

Where a source disagrees with another, we say so explicitly in the Echo body. Where claims cannot be verified across multiple sources, the Echo is held until they can be — or published with an explicit confidence qualifier.

If a source has retracted, corrected, or updated a claim we cited, the Echo is amended within 24 hours and an update note appears on the Echo's revision log. See methodology for the full workflow.

Questions, mostly answered

Common questions about membership.

What's the difference between free and member access?
Free users see every market, every public Echo summary, and can place predictions. Members get the full editorial briefing on each market (not the preview), the complete set of historical parallels (not just the headline), early access 24 hours before public, and detailed portfolio analytics. The free tier is genuinely useful — membership is for people who want depth.
Is membership required to place real-money predictions?
No. Real-money predictions (once Hunch is UKGC-licensed) are open to all verified users, member or not. Membership is about reading depth, not prediction access. Many members never put money in play — they value the analysis and track record.
Can I cancel anytime?
Yes. Monthly memberships can be cancelled at any point and you'll keep access until the end of your billing period. Annual memberships can be cancelled with a pro-rata refund on the unused months. No questions, no friction.
Is there a free trial?
14 days free for both monthly and annual plans. You won't be charged until day 15, and you can cancel any time during the trial without charge.
How is this different from a newspaper subscription?
Newspapers tell you what happened. Hunch lets you predict what will happen — and tracks how often you were right. Membership adds the depth: the historical context behind each prediction, the editorial reasoning, and the tools to measure your own judgement over time.
Are there any group or corporate plans?
Yes, for newsrooms, hedge funds, policy teams, and university departments. Group access starts at 5 seats. Get in touch at members@byhunch.com for pricing.
When does Hunch launch?
The free product opens with the public launch this September. Members get access from launch day. Founding-member rates lock in for as long as you remain subscribed — no price increases for early supporters.

d.title: A new kind of analytical media
d.lead: Hunch is a UK political prediction publishing platform. We pair editorial analysis with prediction markets — same mechanics as Polymarket, completely different product. Built for broadsheet readers who want to read first and predict second.
d.body:
What we do

Hunch publishes Echoes — analytical pieces that combine three things: a current UK political event, the historical pattern it fits, and a market question derived from that pattern. Each Echo is built on 125 years of news archives, cross-referenced across 30+ publications, and double-verified before publication.

Readers can predict the outcome of any Echo using Hunch Points — a skill-based prediction layer that rewards accuracy over time. From 2027, real-money markets become available pending UK Gambling Commission approval.

Why we exist

UK political content has two extremes. On one side, broadsheet analysis — deep but with no way to act on insight. On the other, betting platforms — actionable but with no editorial depth. Hunch fits the gap: rigorous editorial that ends with a prediction, owned by you, scored over time.

Our premise: readers want more than to consume political news. They want to test their own thinking against the patterns. They want their accuracy public. They want to be early to consequential events, not commentary after the fact.

Who reads Hunch

Broadsheet readers, 45+. People who already subscribe to FT, Times, Telegraph, Guardian, Economist. People who follow Westminster closely. People who form views and want a place to test them.

We are not building for crypto-native traders. We are not building for casual punters. We are building for serious people who treat politics as something worth reading carefully — and who want to know whether their reading was correct.

How we are different

  • Publishing-first. Echoes are the atomic unit. Markets are derived from Echoes, not the other way around.
  • Pattern library. 125 years of UK political archives, organised into recurring dynamics with case banks. This is our IP.
  • Public reputation. Predictions are public. Accuracy is tracked via Brier score. Leaderboards make standing visible.
  • Editorial discipline. Every claim cited. No direct opinion. Double-verified. Editorial Code of Practice applies to every piece.
  • UK-first, then Europe. Vertical focus year one: UK fiscal and political prediction. Year three: European expansion via country-specific Hunches.

The team

Hunch is built by Pavlo Denysiuk (founder, Ukrainian, 8 years regulated Web3, ex-CEO Lunu Pay) and Alexander (CTO). Backed by editorial advisors and operational support from a multi-agent AI stack. More on the team →

The institution we are building

Our 20-year ambition: become the FT-tier analytical media institution for civic and political decision-making. What Bloomberg did for financial decision-makers in the 1980s and 90s, we intend to do for thoughtful political readers in the 2020s and beyond.

The path: UK political prediction first. European expansion second. Multi-vertical (finance, sports, culture) third. Print, podcast, and physical presence (Hunch House) over time.

This is a long project. We invite readers who want to be part of it from the start.

Become a Founding Member Read our methodology

Frequently asked

What is a Hunch Point and what does it cost?

Hunch Points are skill-based credits used to make predictions. Free to use, free to earn. They cannot be exchanged for money or goods. They're how we track your forecasting accuracy without involving real money. More on methodology.

Is Hunch licensed by the UK Gambling Commission?

UKGC application is pending. Until licence approval, all markets use Hunch Points only. Real-money services launch on UKGC approval (expected 2027). Licence status.

How is my Brier score calculated?

Brier score measures probabilistic accuracy. A perfect forecaster scores 0; a coin-flip scores 0.25; reliably wrong scores 1. We use the standard mean squared error formula over your resolved predictions. See leaderboard.

Can I delete my account and data?

Yes, anytime from your dashboard. Account data deleted within 30 days. Predictions retained as anonymous statistical record only.

How are Echoes resolved — who decides?

Every Echo's market has a resolution criterion published at creation. When the criterion is met (or the deadline passes), resolution is automatic where possible (government data, named event outcomes), or reviewed by editor where judgement is required. Disputed resolutions go through a public appeal process. Methodology.

d.title: Accessibility statement
d.lead: Hunch aims to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. We will know when we fall short of that and welcome feedback when we do.
d.body:
WCAG 2.1 AA · target

Conformance

This site is designed to conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA. We test on each design release using automated tooling (axe-core) and manual keyboard / screen-reader checks. Known issues are listed below.

What we have built for

  • Full keyboard navigation, including off-canvas menus and predict buttons
  • Visible focus rings on all interactive elements
  • Colour contrast meeting AA against the dark palette (text 4.5:1, large text 3:1)
  • Semantic HTML headings for screen-reader navigation
  • ALT text on all informational images; decorative SVGs marked aria-hidden
  • Forms labelled with explicit <label> tags and aria-describedby for error states
  • Skip-link to main content from every page (in progress)
  • Respect for prefers-reduced-motion for animations and transitions
  • Theme toggle: Light / Dark, with persistence (in progress)

Known issues we are working on

  • Date filter selects on Archive page do not announce changes to screen readers — fix in next sprint
  • Some Echo card hover-only colour shifts not yet duplicated as keyboard-focus styles
  • Light theme variants of several secondary pages pending

Compatibility

We test on:

  • Screen readers: VoiceOver (macOS, iOS), NVDA (Windows), TalkBack (Android)
  • Browsers: Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge — current and one previous version
  • Zoom up to 200% without horizontal scroll

Report an accessibility issue

If you encounter an accessibility barrier on hunch.uk, please tell us. We aim to respond within 48 hours.

Email: accessibility@byhunch.com
Please include: the page URL, what you were trying to do, what went wrong, and the assistive technology you were using.

Enforcement

If you contact us about an accessibility issue and are not satisfied with our response, you may contact the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) or, in Northern Ireland, the Equality Commission for Northern Ireland (ECNI).

Statement preparation

This statement was prepared on 5 June 2026 and is reviewed quarterly.

Last updated: 5 June 2026 · Version 1.0 · Data controller: Krok Group Ltd

TL;DR

We collect the minimum data needed to run Hunch. We never sell your data. We never share it with third-party advertisers. Email is private. Display name and predictions are public. You can export or delete your data at any time.

What we collect

Email address
For login, account notifications, newsletter. Private. Never sold.
Display name
Public. Appears on leaderboard and beside your predictions.
Predictions & Brier score
Public. The point of the product is your public record.
Login & security data
Hashed password, sessions, IP address (logged for 30 days for security only).
Usage analytics
Pages viewed, anonymised. Self-hosted analytics. No third-party trackers.
Payment data (Members)
Processed by Stripe. We store only billing reference and plan. We never see card numbers.

What we don't collect

  • Phone number (unless you choose to share for 2FA)
  • Physical address (unless required for paid services)
  • Third-party advertising identifiers
  • Cross-site browsing behaviour
  • Social-graph data beyond your own connections within the platform

How we use your data

  • Provide the service (account, predictions, leaderboard)
  • Send service emails (account, security, important changes)
  • Send newsletter (only if you opt in; one-click unsubscribe in every email)
  • Maintain security and prevent fraud
  • Improve the product through aggregated, anonymised analytics
  • Comply with legal obligations (regulators, court orders where compelled)

Third parties we use

  • Stripe — payment processing (Members only)
  • Email provider — transactional email and newsletter delivery
  • Hosting provider — cloud infrastructure (data resident in EU/UK)

We have data processing agreements with each. Full vendor list available on request.

Your rights under UK GDPR

  • Access — request a copy of your data
  • Rectification — correct inaccurate data
  • Erasure — delete your account and associated data
  • Portability — export your data in machine-readable format
  • Objection — object to processing for specific purposes
  • Withdraw consent — for marketing/newsletter at any time

Exercise any of these from your dashboard or by writing to privacy@byhunch.com. We respond within 30 days.

Cookies

We use only essential cookies (login session, security, theme preference). No third-party advertising cookies. No tracking pixels. Full cookie list at /cookies.

Data retention

  • Account data: kept while account is active, deleted within 30 days of closure
  • Predictions: retained as part of public record (anonymised after account deletion)
  • Logs and security data: 30 days
  • Financial records: 7 years (UK statutory requirement)

International transfers

Your data is stored in the UK and EU. Any transfers outside happen under UK GDPR-compliant safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses).

Children

Hunch is for 18+ only. We do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 18.

Complaints

If you believe we've handled your data improperly, write to privacy@byhunch.com. You may also lodge a complaint with the UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk.

Changes to this policy

Material changes will be notified by email and in your dashboard at least 30 days before they take effect. Version history available on request.

d.lead: What you may and may not do on Hunch. This sits alongside our Terms of Service and is enforced as part of the same contract.
d.body:
Last updated: 5 June 2026 · Version 1.0

Predicting in good faith

Predictions on Hunch should be your own judgement. The product loses meaning if predictions are gamed.

  • One account per person. Multi-accounting forfeits all Hunch Points and rankings.
  • No coordinated manipulation of market prices through groups, bot networks, or scripts.
  • No use of automated tools to make predictions on your behalf without disclosure.
  • No insider trading: if you have non-public information about a market's outcome (e.g. you are an employee of the entity in question), do not predict on it.

Speaking on the platform

Hunch has light community features — comments on Echoes, public profile, prediction reasoning. These follow standard civility rules.

  • No harassment, threats, or abuse directed at any person or group.
  • No content unlawful in the UK (e.g. defamation, incitement, contempt of court).
  • No doxxing — do not publish private information about others without consent.
  • No spam, repeated promotion of unrelated services, or commercial activity outside our official Partners programme.

Technical use

  • No attempting to reverse-engineer, scrape, or bypass rate limits on the platform.
  • No automated access except via our official API with a valid token.
  • No attempts to compromise security — vulnerability research should be disclosed to security@byhunch.com first.

Real-money services (when live)

Once real-money markets launch under UKGC licence:

  • Funds must come from your own bank account, not third parties.
  • No money-laundering activity. We are required to report suspicious patterns.
  • Withdrawals subject to identity verification and source-of-funds checks above thresholds.
  • If you self-exclude, the period cannot be lifted on request — we are bound by the GAMSTOP framework.

Consequences

Breaches result in actions proportionate to severity:

  • Minor: warning, content removed, points adjustment.
  • Material: temporary suspension, forfeiture of Hunch Points, removal from leaderboard.
  • Serious or repeated: permanent ban, account closure, refund of unused balances minus any sums forfeited under these terms.

Where breach involves potential illegality, we co-operate with UK authorities.

Appeals

If you believe an enforcement action is incorrect, write to appeals@byhunch.com. Appeals are reviewed by a different person from the original decision-maker. Response within 14 days.

Reporting abuse

To report a breach of this policy by another user or content on the platform: trust@byhunch.com. We respond within 48 hours, sooner for urgent safety concerns.

d.title: Editorial Code of Practice
d.body:
Contents
  1. Preamble
  2. Editorial Independence
  3. The AI as a Conscientious Assistant
  4. Information Purity & Sources
  5. Accuracy & Corrections
  6. Market Integrity
  7. Conflicts of Interest
  8. Right of Reply
  9. Privacy & Subjects
  10. Complaints
  11. Algorithmic Transparency
  12. Oversight
  13. The Pledge
Editorial Standards

Editorial Code of Practice

Status
Draft v1
Drafted
22 May 2026
Owner
Founder & Editor — Pavlo Denysiuk
Review
Annual, or sooner upon material change to product, team, or AI pipeline

§Preamble

Hunch exists to bring clarity to a world saturated with information that is wrong, repetitive, or designed to manipulate.

Our readers want two things from the news cycle. They want to test their convictions against reality — to know whether what they already believe is true. And they want to discover the parts of a story that the headlines missed, the precedents that the commentary did not surface, the patterns that arrange themselves only when someone takes the time to look.

We serve both motives with the same product. We do this through Echo — an analytical unit that pairs a current event with the historical patterns that explain it, and from which prediction markets are derived. The markets are not the point. The markets are a measurement instrument that turns conviction into something accountable.

The medium we have chosen is unusual. Prediction markets attract the worst impulses as readily as the best ones: the impulse to enrich oneself through information asymmetry, the impulse to manipulate sentiment for political ends, the impulse to drown legitimate analysis in noise. We are aware of these risks and have built the company to resist them — through editorial discipline, through transparent algorithms, through structural separations between commercial interest and analytical output, and through the rules that follow in this document.

We are also unusual in another respect. The analytical work at Hunch is performed by a team of human editors and by a specifically-trained artificial intelligence that we treat as a colleague. We are proud of this arrangement. We believe AI applied with discipline and humility is one of the most consequential tools any media organisation has ever held — and we believe the standards we hold ourselves to should apply, without exception, to the AI we deploy on the reader's behalf. The AI does not have separate ethics. It has ours.

Information purity is the higher goal. Everything in this Code serves it.

§Section 1Editorial Independence

Editorial decisions at Hunch are made by editors. Commercial considerations — including sponsorship, partnerships, advertising, and the platform's own revenue streams — do not determine which Echoes we publish, what patterns we identify, or what markets we derive.

Specifically:

  • Sponsored content (Paid Echo) is structurally separated from organic editorial. A sponsor of a Paid Echo commissions the topic, sees the draft for factual correction, and is named in a clearly visible label. The sponsor does not write, edit, or approve the analysis. The sponsor cannot prevent publication once commissioned; if a sponsor withdraws before publication, Hunch may publish the same Echo as organic content with no obligation to the sponsor.
  • Hunch's own markets are not editorial subjects. We do not publish analyses that exist to drive volume to a specific market we have a financial interest in beyond the standard service fee that applies to all markets uniformly.
  • No politician, party, lobby group, or commercial entity exercises veto over a Hunch Echo. Subjects of analysis may request factual corrections through the published process (see §7); they have no other channel of influence.

A reader who suspects this principle has been compromised may file a complaint through the process in §9. Such complaints are answered by the founder-editor personally until an independent ombudsperson is appointed (see §11).

§Section 2The AI as a Conscientious Assistant

Hunch operates a specifically-trained artificial intelligence as part of its editorial pipeline. We treat this AI not as a tool but as a colleague held to the same standards as every human on our team. This section describes what the AI does, what it does not do, and what readers are entitled to know.

2.1 What the AI does

  • Scans designated UK news sources on a continuous basis (BBC, Guardian, Reuters, FT, Times, Telegraph, Parliament.uk, ONS, gov.uk, Electoral Commission).
  • Identifies events that meet our publication criteria (binary outcome, machine-verifiable source, concrete resolution date).
  • Drafts the historical-pattern component of each Echo by retrieving comparable precedents from our curated historical database.
  • Suggests resolution criteria and source URLs for derived markets.
  • Performs auto-resolution of markets where the outcome can be determined with ≥95% confidence from official sources, with a second-source check for confidence between 80% and 95%, and a refund-and-cancel path for confidence below 80%.

2.2 What the AI does not do

  • The AI does not place predictions or trade on Hunch markets in any form.
  • The AI does not generate persuasive content designed to move sentiment in a specific direction.
  • The AI does not publish Echoes without an editor's review and approval at launch (we will revisit this only after a sustained period of demonstrated reliability and only with corresponding disclosure).
  • The AI does not draw on private, leaked, or paywalled sources to assert claims of fact; only public, citable sources qualify.
  • The AI is not used to manufacture historical precedents. Every precedent surfaced in an Echo corresponds to a real, sourced event in our database.

2.3 What readers are entitled to know

  • Every Echo carries a disclosure of where AI was used and where editorial judgement was applied. We do not hide either contribution.
  • The historical patterns presented in an Echo include the matching precedents and the dissenting cases. We do not curate away inconvenient counter-examples.
  • The confidence level on auto-resolved markets is published alongside the resolution.
  • The source URLs that drove the AI's analysis are accessible from the Echo page.
  • When the AI is wrong, we say so under the same correction policy that applies to human errors (§4). The AI's mistakes are not hidden behind a system update.

We are proud of our AI deployment. The pride is conditional on the discipline we hold it to.

§Section 3Information Purity and Source Standards

Every Echo is grounded in primary sources. The standard is:

  • Three to five primary sources per Echo, identified explicitly and accessible to the reader where possible.
  • Source hierarchy: statutory and parliamentary publications (Hansard, legislation.gov.uk), official statistical releases (ONS, BoE, DMO), regulatory publications (Ofcom, FCA, UKGC, Ofgem), Electoral Commission filings — before secondary commentary.
  • Editorial commentary (Bloomberg, FT, The Economist, broadsheet op-eds) may be cited as context, never as the source of a factual claim.
  • Tabloid and social-media reporting may be cited as a signal that a story is in circulation, never as a source of fact.

When a fact cannot be sourced to the above standard, it does not enter an Echo. Speculation framed as fact is the exact information pollution we exist to push back against.

Hunch is a complement to journalism, not a substitute. The reporting produced by broadsheet publications — including the Financial Times, The Times, The Guardian, and The Economist — is essential context for the work we do. Our citations of it are visible, our links to it are generous, and we never republish or rewrite. Where our analysis builds on a reporter's work, we say so plainly and send our readers to read the original. We compete with no one on the speed of journalism; we offer something different — historical pattern depth, and a measurement instrument for conviction.

§Section 4Accuracy and Corrections

When an Echo contains a factual error, we correct it. The standard process is:

  • Errors are corrected at the source — the Echo is edited to remove the inaccuracy.
  • A correction note is published at the top of the Echo identifying what was wrong, what is now correct, and the date of the correction.
  • The original version is preserved in an edit log accessible from the Echo footer.
  • Where the error affected the resolution of a market, the market is re-resolved or refunded, and affected participants are notified directly.

There is no shame in a correction. There is shame in concealing one.

The same policy applies to AI-generated content. When the AI is wrong, the correction note names the AI's contribution explicitly. We do not allow an AI mistake to be quietly attributed to "a system update."

§Section 5Market Integrity and Insider-Trading Prevention

Hunch operates prediction markets as a measurement instrument for conviction. The integrity of those markets is therefore an editorial concern as much as a commercial one.

We commit to the following protections:

  • Short resolution windows — most markets run between one and thirty days. Long-horizon markets create insider opportunity; we avoid them.
  • Public resolution sources only — every market resolves against an officially published outcome (Hansard, legislation.gov.uk, ONS, BoE, gov.uk). We do not resolve against "sources say" reporting or leaked documents.
  • Volume limits per market per user — individual exposure to a single market is capped to make insider extraction uneconomic. Specific caps are published.
  • Anomaly detection — sharp shifts in conviction combined with large positions from new accounts are flagged for human review. Suspect activity is suspended pending investigation.
  • Time-weighted scoring — predictions made earlier (when uncertainty was higher) carry more reputational weight than late predictions. This rewards genuine insight, not late-stage insider knowledge.
  • Algorithmic transparency — readers have access to the same historical database the AI draws on. The AI does not operate on private data unavailable to readers.

A platform that profits from prediction is structurally tempted to ignore manipulation. Hunch will not.

§Section 6Conflicts of Interest

The following rules bind everyone employed by, contracted to, or holding equity in Hunch:

  • No trading on Hunch markets by Hunch staff, contractors, board members, or material equity holders.
  • No directing of family members to trade on Hunch markets on their behalf.
  • Personal political donations and party memberships must be disclosed to the founder-editor. They do not disqualify staff from working on any topic, but they are kept on file and may be cited in a published byline if the conflict is material.
  • Outside writing or commentary by Hunch staff on political topics covered by Hunch must be disclosed. Hunch retains the right to require a disclosure note on the external piece.
  • Gifts, hospitality, and paid travel from any party with an interest in markets we cover must be declined or reported.

These rules apply to the AI by extension: the systems we train cannot be augmented with data feeds, weights, or fine-tuning that introduce an undeclared bias. Where the AI is trained, the training source is documented.

§Section 7Right of Reply

Subjects of an Echo — politicians, organisations, public officials, and named private individuals — may request factual corrections through a published process. We commit to:

  • A response from a named editor within five working days of receipt.
  • Correction at source where a factual error is established, under §4.
  • A right of reply published below the Echo where a subject contests a characterisation we have made about them, even if no factual error is identified, and we judge the matter to be of material public interest.
  • No editing of the published Echo to remove material on commercial or relationship grounds outside of this process.

We do not extend right of reply to anonymous parties or to entities seeking to suppress legitimate analysis.

§Section 8Privacy and Subjects of Analysis

The default for Hunch coverage is the political and economic public sphere — actions of public officials in their public capacity, votes recorded in Parliament, statements made on the record, decisions published by regulators. Private life is not Hunch's subject.

  • Named private individuals appear only where directly material (e.g. a named donor whose role is publicly documented). They are subject to the same right of reply (§7).
  • Vulnerable persons — children, persons in distress, persons under investigation but not charged — are not subjects of Echo coverage unless an overriding public interest is identified and explicitly noted.
  • Subjects of prediction markets that resolve based on personal events (e.g. a resignation, a court appearance) require an editor's explicit judgement that the market is in the public interest and based on publicly verifiable resolution criteria.

We do not run markets on the private lives of private individuals.

§Section 9Complaints

A reader who believes Hunch has fallen short of this Code may file a complaint via:

  • Email: complaints@byhunch.com
  • Published form: byhunch.com/complaints (linked from every Echo footer)

We commit to:

  • Acknowledgement within two working days.
  • A substantive response from a named editor within ten working days.
  • An escalation path: if the complainant is not satisfied with the editor's response, the complaint may be escalated to the founder-editor (initially Pavlo Denysiuk), and from the appointment of an independent ombudsperson (see §11), to that ombudsperson.

Complaints, anonymised, are reported in aggregate in Hunch's annual transparency report.

§Section 10Algorithmic Transparency

In addition to the AI-use disclosures in §2, Hunch publishes:

  • The list of news sources monitored by our scanning system.
  • The list of resolution sources used by our auto-resolution engine.
  • The confidence thresholds (95% / 80%) and the actions triggered at each threshold.
  • The historical database structure (event, year, category, outcome) — not every record is public, but the schema and the aggregate volume are.
  • The volume, anomaly detection, and time-weighted scoring rules in summary form.

Where a reader requests further detail on a specific algorithmic decision — for example, "why did the AI surface these three precedents and not other comparable ones?" — we commit to responding within ten working days where the underlying logic can be disclosed without compromising market integrity.

§Section 11Oversight

This Code is enforced by the founder-editor of Hunch. In Year 1 that is Pavlo Denysiuk. The founder-editor is accountable for every breach of this Code and for the integrity of every Echo published.

  • From Year 2: Hunch will appoint a three-person Editorial Advisory Board including at least one member with a working background in UK political journalism or analysis, and at least one with a background in AI governance or research ethics.
  • From Year 3 (or earlier if growth permits): Hunch will appoint an independent ombudsperson with the authority to investigate complaints, publish findings, and require corrections under this Code.
  • Annual transparency report: Hunch publishes an annual report identifying material errors corrected, complaints received and resolved, AI confidence-threshold performance, and any material breaches of this Code.

External accountability we may opt into as the company matures includes IPSO (Independent Press Standards Organisation) registration; we will consider that pathway once the company has a permanent editorial team beyond the founder.

§Section 12The Pledge

Every person employed by, contracted to, or holding equity in Hunch is asked to read this Code at induction and to confirm their understanding of and commitment to it.

The same expectation applies to the artificial intelligence we operate. The systems we deploy are trained on the principles of this Code, evaluated against it, and corrected when their behaviour falls short. We are proud of our AI not because it is powerful but because we have taught it to be useful within the disciplines that follow from this document.

Information purity is the higher goal.
We commit to it together — humans and the AI we are proud to call our colleague.

This Code is reviewed annually and on any material change to the product, team, or AI pipeline. The current version is always available at byhunch.com/editorial-code. The full revision history is published alongside.

Hunch is operated by Krok Group Ltd. Company No. 17183343. Registered in England & Wales.

d.title: Stay in control
d.lead: Hunch is built to be read first, predicted second. Before real-money services launch (subject to UKGC licence), here is the toolkit we will operate.
d.body:
Real-money markets are not yet live

All current predictions use Hunch Points only. Hunch Points cannot be exchanged for money or goods. Real-money services launch on UKGC licence approval. The framework below applies from day one.

If predicting stops being fun

For most people, prediction is a way to test thinking against reality. For some, it stops being that. If you feel any of the following, take action:

  • Thinking about your predictions when you should be doing other things
  • Spending more time or money on prediction than you intended
  • Predicting to chase losses or recover lost points
  • Hiding your prediction activity from people close to you
  • Predicting when stressed, low, or after drinking

Tools we offer on the platform

Daily session limits

Set a maximum number of predictions per day or a maximum time spent on the platform. The platform soft-locks after the limit and prompts a 24-hour cool-down.

Deposit limits (real-money phase)

Once real-money services are live, set deposit caps per day, week, or month. Increases require a 24-hour cooling period; decreases take effect immediately.

Self-exclusion

Pause your account for any period from 24 hours to 5 years. Self-exclusion is irreversible within the chosen period — we cannot lift it on request. Account, predictions, and email all paused.

Reality check pop-ups

Every 30 minutes of active session time, the platform shows a brief summary of your activity and a Take a break button.

GAMSTOP integration

If you're registered with the UK national self-exclusion scheme GAMSTOP, our platform will detect and block sign-up automatically once real-money services launch.

UK help organisations

GamCare
0808 8020 133
Free, confidential, 24/7. England, Scotland, Wales. gamcare.org.uk
National Gambling Helpline
0808 8020 133
24/7, run by GamCare. Phone, chat, WhatsApp.
BeGambleAware
begambleaware.org
Independent resources, advice, treatment finder.
GAMSTOP
gamstop.co.uk
UK national self-exclusion scheme for all licensed operators.

Age verification

Hunch is for 18+ only. Real-money services require government-issued ID verification at first deposit. Hunch Points (current phase) require account age 18+ on signup.

Operator commitments

We do not target advertising at under-18s. We do not advertise during live sports broadcasts. We do not use bonus offers tied to volume. We do not contact self-excluded users.
